facts.fact_text: The three applicants in the present case were involved in a number of public events in 2007-2008 in Rostov-na-Donu.
Some of the applications lodged by the three applicants concern the same public events.
On 24 November 2007 Mr Nagibin proceeded with the static demonstration (picket).

On 19 June 2007 Mr Nagibin and Mr Ye. notified the Rostov-na-Donu town administration of their intention to hold a meeting of approximately three hundred participants on Sovetov Square from 5 p.m. to 6 p.m. on 30 June 2007.

On 19 June 2007 Mr Nagibin and Mr Ye. notified the Rostov-na-Donu town administration of their intention to hold the 'Dissenters' March' (Марш несогласных) along Sadovaya and Sovetskaya Streets following the meeting on Sovetov Square on 30 June 2007.
On 19 June 2007 Mr Nagibin and Mr Ye. notified the Rostov-na-Donu town administration of their intention to hold another meeting at Karl Marx Square until 7.30 p.m. on 30 June 2007.
At 5.20 p.m. on 12 December 2008 Mr Nagibin came to Voroshilovskiy Drive for a solitary demonstration.
Mr Nagibin carried a sandwich board during his solitary demonstration on 12 December 2008 at Voroshilovskiy Drive.
Mr Nagibin distributed leaflets to passers-by during his solitary demonstration on 12 December 2008 at Voroshilovskiy Drive.
Mr Nagibin was taken to the Kirovskiy district police station following his apprehension on 12 December 2008.
The case concerns restrictions imposed by the authorities on the location of several public events.
The case concerns restrictions imposed by the authorities on the time of conduct of several public events.
The case concerns restrictions imposed by the authorities on the manner of conduct of several public events.
The applicants complained about being unlawfully arrested.
The applicants complained about being convicted of various administrative offences.

On 24 November 2007 Mr Nagibin was apprehended because his passport was found to be defiled with unauthorised pen writing and the police officers intended to draft the relevant record of the administrative offence at the police station.
Mr Nagibin was brought to a police station and charged with non-compliance with a lawful order of a police officer under Article 19.3 § 1 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The Rostov-na-Donu town administration imposed restrictions as to the location of the public event on each occasion that Mr Nikolayev submitted a notification.

Mr Nagibin was charged with a breach of public order and verbal assaults, an administrative offence under Article 20.1 § 1 of the Code of Administrative Offences, following his apprehension on 12 December 2008.

On 22 June 2007 the Justice of the Peace of the 4th Circuit of the Pervomayskiy District of Rostov-na-Donu found Mr Nagibin guilty of a breach of public order, an administrative offence under Article 20.1 § 1 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
Mr Nagibin was sentenced to nine days' administrative imprisonment by the Justice of the Peace of the 4th Circuit of the Pervomayskiy District of Rostov-na-Donu on 22 June 2007.

At the Pervomayskiy district police station, a report on an administrative offence under Article 19.3 of the Code of Administrative Offences (failure to comply with lawful demands of a police officer) was drawn up against Mr Nagibin.

The Pervomayskiy District Court of Rostov-na-Donu found that the police officers had acted within their competence because they had the right, under section 11 §§ 2 and 15 of the Police Act, to check the identity papers of individuals suspected of a criminal or administrative offence.

The Pervomayskiy District Court of Rostov-na-Donu found that Mr Nagibin's overnight detention had been lawful because the Code of Administrative Offences permitted detention for up to forty-eight hours.

On 2 December 2007 Mr Nagibin was convicted of the administrative offence of non-compliance with a lawful order of a police officer on the basis of the police report and oral testimony of officer Mr Kh.
Mr Nagibin was sentenced to three days of administrative imprisonment.

On 13 December 2008 the Justice of the Peace of the 6th Court Circuit of the Kirovskiy District found Mr Nagibin guilty of breach of public order and verbal assaults under Article 20.1 § 1 of the Code of Administrative Offences.
The Justice of the Peace sentenced Mr Nagibin to three days' administrative imprisonment, to be calculated from 7.35 p.m. on 12 December 2008.
The police officers testified that they had received operative information on the preparation by National-Bolsheviks of an unlawful march in Moscow, known as the 'Dissenters' March'.
The police officers testified that they were requested to conduct explanatory and preventive discussions with prospective participants in the 'Dissenters' March', including Mr Nagibin.

The Pervomayskiy District Court of Rostov-na-Donu found that the police officers had acted within their competence because they had the right, under section 11 §§ 2 and 15 of the Police Act, to check the identity papers of individuals suspected of a criminal or administrative offence.
The Justice of the Peace based her decision on statements by two witnesses who had signed their statements attesting that Mr Nagibin used foul language and verbally assaulted them.
The Justice of the Peace rejected Mr Nagibin's request to question the prosecution witnesses.

By decision of 18 July 2007, the Pervomayskiy District Court refused to examine Mr Nagibin's complaint about the decision to conduct 'preventive discussions', finding that the issues raised had already been determined in the judgment of 6 April 2007.
On 17 November 2007 the Pervomayskiy District Court's decision of 18 July 2007 refusing to examine Mr Nagibin's complaint about 'preventive discussions' was upheld on appeal.
The Rostov-na-Donu town administration noted that the notification did not indicate which side of Sadovaya and Sovetskaya Streets the march would take place.
The Rostov-na-Donu town administration noted that the notification did not indicate where the participants would cross the streets.
The Rostov-na-Donu Regional Court held on 21 November 2007 that the organisers had not made use of the possibility to submit more detailed information on the route and venue.

The Justice of the Peace of the 6th Court Circuit of the Kirovskiy District based the conviction on submissions by several witnesses and two police officers, establishing in general terms that Mr Nagibin had used foul language in a public space.
The text of the judgment of 13 December 2008 did not specify which particular words Mr Nagibin had pronounced.

The Justice of the Peace did not address Mr Nagibin's arguments that he had not used foul language but rather had been making a solo demonstration when the police officers came and ordered him to stop the unlawful demonstration.
Mr Nagibin did not receive any food during his custody at the Pervomayskiy district police station from 12 to 13 December 2006.
Mr Nagibin was not taken outdoors during his custody at the Pervomayskiy district police station from 12 to 13 December 2006.
The cell at the Pervomayskiy district police station where Mr Nagibin was held measured approximately 2 square metres.
The cell at the Pervomayskiy district police station accommodated Mr Nagibin and one other person.
The cell at the Pervomayskiy district police station was not equipped with a bed.
Mr Nagibin shared the administrative-detention cell at the Kirovskiy district police station with three to five other detainees.
The administrative-detention cell at the Kirovskiy district police station was equipped with one bed, thirty centimetres wide and too short for an adult.
Detainees in the administrative-detention cell at the Kirovskiy district police station took turns to sleep on the floor.
There was no natural light in the administrative-detention cell at the Kirovskiy district police station.
There was no possibility for outdoor exercise for detainees held in the administrative-detention cell at the Kirovskiy district police station.
On 27 May 2010 the Rostov Regional Court found that Mr Nagibin was unlawfully deprived of proper meals during his detention at the Kirovskiy district police station from 24 to 26 November 2007.
On 27 May 2010 the Rostov Regional Court found that Mr Nagibin was unlawfully deprived of a sleeping place during his detention at the Kirovskiy district police station from 24 to 26 November 2007.
The domestic courts established that Mr Nagibin was kept in a cell measuring 3.5 square metres with three other persons during his detention at the Kirovskiy district police station.
Mr Nagibin argued that he had no sleeping place during his detention at the Kirovskiy district police station in the night from 12 to 13 December 2008.
Mr Nagibin argued that on 13 December 2008 he was transported in an unheated minivan for more than two hours.
Mr Nagibin argued that he had not received any food on 13 December 2008.
The Pervomayskiy District Court found on 25 March 2009 that Mr Nagibin had been provided with a sleeping place on a bench and bed linen during his detention at the Kirovskiy district police station.
The Pervomayskiy District Court found on 25 March 2009 that Mr Nagibin had been given packed food provisions on 12 and 13 December 2008.
